title: Extending a finite-type quasi-coherent submodule from an open algebraic subspace
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. A space is quasi-compact if it admits a surjective etale atlas from a quasi-compact scheme, and quasi-separated if its absolute diagonal is quasi-compact on scheme tests. An open subspace means a representable open immersion, tested on schemes using [def-weil-open-immersion]. Let $X$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated and let $W\subseteq X$ be a quasi-compact open subspace. Use sheaves of modules on the small etale site with its structure sheaf [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-trf-algebraic-space] and quasi-coherence of [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. For such a sheaf $\mathcal M$, its restriction to $W$ is the sheaf on $W_{\mathrm{et}}$ with $\mathcal M|_W(T)=\mathcal M(T)$ for each etale scheme $T\to W$, using its composite to $X$. A submodule sheaf means a subsheaf whose sections on every etale scheme object form a submodule of the ambient sections. Finite type means etale locally generated by finitely many sections. Let $\mathcal F$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module and let $\mathcal G\subseteq\mathcal F|_W$ be a finite-type quasi-coherent submodule sheaf. There exists a finite-type quasi-coherent submodule sheaf $\mathcal G'\subseteq\mathcal F$ such that $\mathcal G'|_W=\mathcal G$ as submodule sheaves of $\mathcal F|_W$.

proof.text: Let $j:W\hookrightarrow X$ be the inclusion. The atlas and point-topology notions of quasi-compactness agree by [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image]. Therefore [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-permanence] applies to the quasi-compact source $W$ and quasi-separated target $X$, and makes $j$ quasi-compact. Also $W\times_XW=W$ since $W$ is a subfunctor, so the diagonal of $j$ is the identity. On every scheme test the identity is a closed immersion: its image is the whole closed subset and its structure-sheaf map is the identity, hence surjective [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Thus $j$ is separated. Apply [lem-trf-space-qc-separated-quasi-coherent-pushforward] to $\mathcal G$ and $\mathcal F|_W$ to obtain quasi-coherent $j_*\mathcal G$ and $j_*(\mathcal F|_W)$. Restriction of a local presentation shows that $\mathcal F|_W$ is quasi-coherent, so both applications have the required module hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0853 (lemma-extend), first three proof sentences; spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 073B (lemma-quasi-compact-quasi-separated-permanence), (1), and Tag 03M9 (lemma-pushforward).

proof.text: Use the canonical direct image and adjunction unit of [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. Write $i:j_*\mathcal G\to j_*(\mathcal F|_W)$ for the map induced by the given inclusion and $r:\mathcal F\to j_*(\mathcal F|_W)$ for restriction. Set $\mathcal H=\ker(i-r:j_*\mathcal G\oplus\mathcal F\to j_*(\mathcal F|_W))$. The direct sum and kernel are quasi-coherent by [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-kernels-colimits]. The map $i$ is injective: on a test scheme a compatible family in $\mathcal G$ which maps to zero has every chart component zero. Hence the projection $p:\mathcal H\to\mathcal F$ is injective, since a pair $(g,0)$ in its kernel satisfies $i(g)=0$. For an etale scheme $T\to W$, the direct-image chart limit is just sections over $T$: the compatible family is determined by its component on the chart $T$, and every other component is its restriction. Thus $r|_W$ is the identity and $\mathcal H|_W$ consists of pairs $(g,f)$ with $f$ equal to the image of $g$. Projection to $g$ gives $\mathcal H|_W\cong\mathcal G$, under which $p|_W$ is exactly the prescribed inclusion into $\mathcal F|_W$.

source.place: Tag 0853 (lemma-extend), kernel construction and equality on the open; spaces-properties.tex Tag 03M1 (lemma-properties-quasi-coherent), (1),(3).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-module-fp-directed-approximation] to the quasi-coherent $\mathcal H$ on the quasi-compact quasi-separated $X$. Obtain a small filtered diagram of finitely presented quasi-coherent modules $\mathcal E_a$ and a colimit cocone $e_a:\mathcal E_a\to\mathcal H$ in all module sheaves. Each $\mathcal E_a$ is of finite type: in a local finite presentation the images of the finitely many standard basis sections generate. Choose one affine surjective etale chart $T=\operatorname{Spec}A\to W$ by [lem-trf-space-qc-finite-affine-atlas-refinement]. Its composite to $X$ is an etale chart as in the restriction convention of the statement. By [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-affine-chart-calculus], evaluation on $T$ computes this filtered colimit, so $\mathcal H(T)=\varinjlim_a\mathcal E_a(T)$. Moreover $\mathcal H(T)=\mathcal G(T)$ is a finitely generated $A$-module, by the same affine-chart finite-type criterion on $W$.

source.place: Tag 0853 (lemma-extend), finite-type selection; Tag 0829 (lemma-directed-colimit-finite-type), proof using images of a finitely presented approximation, and Tag 086Y (lemma-finite-directed-colimit-surjective-maps), first proof paragraph.

proof.text: Choose finitely many generators of $\mathcal H(T)$. Every element of a filtered colimit of modules has a representative at some stage. Lift each generator and take a common receiving stage $a$ for their finitely many stages; their images show that $e_a(T)$ is surjective. If there are no generators, choose any object of the nonempty filtered category. The cokernel $\mathcal C$ of $e_a$ is quasi-coherent by [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-kernels-colimits], its restriction to $W$ is the cokernel of $e_a|_W$, and [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-affine-chart-calculus] computes its sections on $T$ as this zero cokernel. The affine correspondence makes its restriction to $T$ zero. A sheaf zero on a surjective etale cover is zero (sections vanish after a covering and the separatedness axiom then makes them zero). Thus $e_a|_W$ is an epimorphism.

source.place: Tag 086Y (lemma-finite-directed-colimit-surjective-maps), finite generators lifted to a common stage; Tag 0853 (lemma-extend), selection sentence, with the finite-generation argument made explicit.

proof.text: Define $\mathcal G'=\operatorname{Im}(\mathcal E_a\xrightarrow{e_a}\mathcal H\xrightarrow{p}\mathcal F)$, with its canonical inclusion into $\mathcal F$. It is quasi-coherent by [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-kernels-colimits]. On each affine etale chart its module is the image of the corresponding module map by [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-affine-chart-calculus]. The source has finitely generated sections there; the images of any finite generating family generate its image. The affine-chart finite-type criterion therefore makes $\mathcal G'$ finite type. On every affine etale chart over $W$, this same image calculation computes the restriction of $\mathcal G'$ as the image of $p|_W\circ e_a|_W$. Step 4 makes $e_a|_W$ epi, and step 2 identifies $p|_W$ with the prescribed inclusion of $\mathcal G$. Its image is exactly $\mathcal G$, as a submodule of $\mathcal F|_W$. These chartwise equalities of subsheaves agree on restrictions and hence give $\mathcal G'|_W=\mathcal G$, with the required inclusion, rather than just an abstract isomorphism.
